top.line: Time first, from the job you have
top.para: A startup needs time before money. Treat it as art, with money as a side effect. Start from your own revenue stream, start while employed, ask for part time, and treat savings, an exit or debt as buying time. Take investment later, and avoid regret.

in-short.line: Find time, buy time, and do not regret it
in-short.para: Time is the resource. Improve the revenue you already have, cut streaming, start in a job, negotiate part time, and accept debt as a way to buy time, as Dinis did. There has never been a better time.

time.line: A startup is all-consuming, like art
time.para: Funding depends on circumstances, but the main need is time. A founder is a creator who loves the work; money should follow success, not drive it, so the question is how to find time while earning a living.

revenue.line: Make your existing revenue stream better first
revenue.para: The best start is using the technology to improve work you already do, or selling to people you know. Even if that is all you achieve, it is a success; solving no real problem means chasing shadows.

more-time.line: Most people have more time than they think
more-time.para: Anyone thinking of a startup usually has some success or few expenses and a drive to create. There is always time, starting with the hours that go to streaming.

job.line: The constraint of a job helps you focus
job.para: Starting while employed gives income and therefore time, and limited hours force focus and shipping. Do it openly, with managers aware, on separate machines, never competing.

part-time.line: Ask to go part time, as Dinis did
part-time.para: Many employers prefer half of a good person to none. Dinis asked to go part time to build things elsewhere, offering a solution, and it worked; if you are not valued, leave anyway.

gamble.line: Debt and an exit, used to buy time
gamble.para: It is a gamble. Dinis cleared his debt, then went back into it for his GenAI startup, and uses exit money to pay himself instead of taking an executive role. Investment comes later, when profitable.

regret.line: Avoid regret; the pool is wider now
regret.para: There has never been a better time to create a company, but more people can, so competition is real. The expert in the problem has the advantage.

limits.para: Debt and an exit are personal. Part time depends on role and employer. Debt buys time only if you can carry it.

sources.line: A memo, and the related articles
sources.para: Dinis's memo of 19 October 2026, with the newsroom's articles on open source, selling, starting a company and funding.
